cases.neutralTitle: Mammogram, both breasts, CC and MLO · CBIS-DDSM P_00021
cases.learnTitle: Mass on CC and MLO mammograms (benign at pathology; mass outline)
cases.referenceSummary: Mass outlined on every view (oval, circumscribed margin (benign; outline)); BI-RADS assessment and pathology as given in the CBIS-DDSM case description. Mass outlines were refined in CBIS-DDSM from the original DDSM contours. Digitised screen-film mammograms, downsampled 2x2; no pixel spacing, so distances are not measurable.
cases.learnNotes: A screening mammogram has two views of each breast: craniocaudal (CC, from above) and mediolateral oblique (MLO, at an angle, with the pectoral muscle along the back of the breast). Hang the two breasts mirror-image, chest walls to the middle, and compare left with right. A real finding should be found on both views; on the MLO a lesion lies at about the same distance from the nipple as on the CC. Describe a mass by its shape (oval, round, irregular), margin (circumscribed, obscured, microlobulated, indistinct, spiculated) and density: irregular, spiculated and dense favors cancer; oval, circumscribed and low density favors a benign lesion. Calcifications are described by form (round, coarse, rod-like and vascular are typically benign; fine pleomorphic and fine linear are suspicious) and distribution (diffuse, regional, grouped, linear, segmental).

tasks.title: Find the mass on both views
tasks.prompt: Read every view, comparing the two breasts. Mark the abnormality on each view where you see it (point, box or outline), or state that you find none.

hints.text: Hang the CC views and the MLO views mirror-image and compare left with right, quadrant by quadrant.
Found it on one view? On the other view it lies at about the same distance from the nipple.

tasks.title: Describe the mass margin
tasks.prompt: Zoom in on the mass on both views. How would you describe its margin?

options.why: Sharp, well-defined edge over most of the outline: favors a benign lesion.
Edge hidden by overlapping normal tissue.
Lines radiating from the edge: the most suspicious margin.

hints.text: Follow the edge of the mass all the way round; spicules are thin lines that radiate out from it.
